view_frame: The drawing presents three orthographic views: BOTTOM (XY), TOP (XY), and FRONT (XZ). The world coordinate system is defined with X as width (left-right), Y as depth (front-back), and Z as height (up-down). The FRONT view displays the XZ plane, showing the height and width profile. The TOP and BOTTOM views display the XY plane, showing the cross-sections at the top and bottom respectively.

features.placement: The solid is centered on the Z-axis. The bottom rectangular profile is located at Z=0 with corners at (±30, ±20). The top circular profile is located at Z=60 with a radius of 15 centered at (0,0). The loft connects these two profiles linearly.
features.evidence: BOTTOM view shows a '60 x 40 mm rectangle'. TOP view shows a 'diameter 30 mm' circle. FRONT view shows a trapezoid labeled 'height 60 mm; solid'.

connections: The rectangular base (60x40) and circular top (diameter 30) are connected by a linear loft transition.
edit_rules: Changing the bottom width (X) or depth (Y) updates the rectangular profile at Z=0.
Changing the top diameter updates the circular profile at Z=60.
Changing the height updates the Z-position of the top profile.
The loft maintains the correspondence between the rectangular and circular profiles without twist.
